answers.question: Is it crazy to do one more 16-miler on Wednesday so I feel ready?
answers.answer: No, please do not do a 16 on Wednesday. Here is the honest version: a 16-miler six days out costs more than it gives. The fitness is already banked from the 20, 17 and 20 in the last five weeks, and a big midweek run cannot add fitness now, it can only leave your legs flat on race day. Heavy, dead legs during a taper are the body soaking up the work you have already done, and almost everyone feels this way the week before a marathon. The right move is to keep runs short, drop in a couple of race-pace miles midweek to remind the legs what 8:35/mi feels like, and arrive Sunday fresh and a little bored. That is how a 3:45 goes well.

new.analysis:
You did the work. Across the last five weeks you built to a 20, held form on a 17, repeated a 20, and finished with a controlled 12 on Sun Oct 11, all at an easy heart rate around 146 with small drift. The engine for under 3:45 is there.

The feeling of losing fitness is the taper doing its job. Mileage drops, the legs refill their stores, and they feel heavy and flat before they feel springy. The run-by-run pace and heart rate have been steady for weeks, which is the signal that matters, not how the legs feel on a Saturday shuffle.

For race week I am keeping volume low, cutting Wed to a short tune-up with a couple of miles at goal pace (around 8:35/mi), and adding strides on Tue so the legs stay quick. Nothing new: same shoes, same fueling, same morning routine as your long runs. No testing kit on race day.

On pace, under 3:45 is 8:35/mi. The sensible plan is to go through 10k a touch slower than that (around 8:40 – 8:45/mi), settle into 8:33 – 8:35 through halfway, and only start pressing after mile 20 if you still feel strong. The classic blow-up is a 7:55 opening mile that feels free, so hold back early even if it feels too easy.

Two small jobs this week: write down your fueling (gels, carbs per hour, when you take them) and check the forecast by Thursday so you can pick the right kit. If anything new flares up in the legs, tell me and we scale back further, not harder.
